ENT Clinical Note – Dr. Smith / Patient: Matt Carter (14 Aug 1989)

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • Six-week history of generalized body aches and marked fatigue beginning ~2 weeks after return from U.S. holiday (end Jan / early Feb).  
  • No clear precipitating event identified; possible outdoor exposure with frequent walking in shorts and boots.

- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Well over Christmas/New Year.  
  • Symptoms began mid-Feb; persistent since.  
  • Rash (see below) appeared mid–late Feb, faded over ~2 weeks; energy levels have remained low.

- ENT symptoms:
  • Denies persistent cold symptoms, earache, nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, ocular itch/watering.  
  • Denies throat tightness/closure, voice change, dysphagia, odynophagia, drooling.  
  • Denies stridor, noisy breathing, dyspnea.  
  • Denies facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling.  
  • Reports one self-limited sore throat at time of rash (mid-Feb).  
  • Denies ear pain/hearing change, neck pain/swelling.

- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • No prior similar prolonged fatigue episodes reported.  
  • No ED visits/hospitalizations for ENT or allergic issues.

- Allergies and current medications:
  • Allergic rhinitis (hay fever); specific allergens not detailed.  
  • No drug or food allergies documented.  
  • Preventative asthma inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented (patient uses “morning and night”).  
  • OTC antihistamine – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • Rescue/reliever inhaler not currently in use.

- Social context:
  • Lives with wife at home; supportive environment.  
  • Works for a health-technology company; reduced daytime energy/concentration but continues working.

Objective:
- Observable findings (video consult):
  • Patient showed photograph of circular rash on posterior calf; appeared erythematous, non-pruritic, resolved.  
- Airway/breathing: No audible distress; patient speaking in full sentences.  
- Mental status: Alert, oriented; reports fatigue but no confusion or syncope.  
- Vitals and physical examination: Not recorded.  
- Accompaniment: Patient alone during call; wife lives with him.

Assessment:
- Prolonged fatigue, myalgias, and resolved erythematous calf rash – suspicious for possible Lyme disease (tick-borne) acquired during U.S. hiking; other causes of systemic fatigue (anemia, thyroid, infection) also considered.
- No current ENT airway compromise or allergic reaction.

Plan:
1. Investigations ordered:
   • Blood tests: complete blood count, renal & liver profile, thyroid function, inflammatory markers, Lyme serology.  
2. Patient instructed to book phlebotomy through support line and arrange follow-up phone appointment ~1 week after tests.  
3. Safety-net advice:
   • Seek urgent medical review (e.g., NHS 111 / A&E) for fevers, worsening fatigue, new rashes, neurological symptoms, or any ENT red-flags (throat swelling, voice change, breathing difficulty).  
4. Education:
   • Discussed potential link between tick exposure and Lyme disease; advised on preventive measures for future outdoor activities (long trousers, insect repellent, prompt tick removal).  
5. Follow-up:
   • Virtual review after blood-test results to confirm diagnosis and initiate treatment (e.g., doxycycline) if indicated.  
   • Routine asthma review recommended at next primary-care visit.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing but expected: comprehensive drug/food allergy list; detailed medication names, doses, devices; vitals and full physical exam.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall; occasional audio dropouts but clinically relevant data captured.
